basisOfRecord.quote: The field study of periodical cicadas was conducted from May to August 2004 on the Princeton University campus (Oberdörster & Grant, 2006a).
These were captured by hand or with a net, or in three instances they were found as eclosing nymphs and kept for 48 h prior to release.
For morphological measurements other specimens were captured by hand.
We report here a morphological study of two species of 17-year cicada, M. cassini and M. septendecim.

lifeStage.quote: Actively flying or singing M. septendecim and M. cassini, members of ‘brood X’ (Williams & Simon, 1995), were captured by hand in May and June.

measurementStatistic.quote: On average, T. chloromera flew three to four times faster than did the two Magicicada species.
A total of 34 M. cassini and 81 M. septendecim flight speeds were recorded.
In total, 178 periodical cicadas (M. septendecim and M. cassini) were measured.

Since repeatability values of all measured traits were high, in the range 0.90–0.99 when samples of 30 individuals were measured twice (Table 1), the adjustment had little effect on the estimates of allometric slopes.
On average, M. cassini flew 27% as fast and M. septendecim flew 29% as fast as did T. chloromera (Fig. 2).
The two Magicicada species had smaller body masses and lower wing loading values than did the three Tibicen species (Table 3).
Allometric coefficients for the aspect ratios of the two Magicicada species and T. chloromera lay mainly between 0.3 and 0.5 (Table 5).
The two Magicicada species were smaller compared with the three Tibicen species, and had smaller aspect ratios.
